title: Chiral symmetry and the orbital susceptibility of disordered honeycomb flakes
abstract: The orbital susceptibility of a small disordered grain is dominated by rare samples in which an occupied and an empty level nearly touch. In a chaotic grain such near-degeneracies are suppressed by level repulsion and must also coincide with the chemical potential, so the mean susceptibility stays finite. In a neutral honeycomb flake, chiral (sublattice) symmetry removes the second condition: It places the chemical potential in the middle of the smallest gap, in every disorder realization. Here we show that the mean orbital susceptibility then grows as $\ln(1/T)$ at low temperature $T$ if disorder can close this gap while a magnetic field still mixes the two levels, and that the hopping geometry decides whether it can: Positive nearest-neighbor hopping on a compact hexagonal flake keeps the gap open, third-neighbor hopping allows it to close. In a chiral random-matrix model with $n$ level pairs the coefficient of the logarithm is $C_n=\sqrt{2/n}\,Γ[(n+1)/2]/Γ(n/2)$, close to unity, and a detuned chemical potential cuts the logarithm off.
summary: This theoretical work determines the mean orbital susceptibility of disordered honeycomb flakes, finding that chiral symmetry leads to a characteristic logarithmic divergence in the susceptibility at low temperatures. This divergence is critically dependent on the hopping geometry allowing the energy gap to close, and it is suppressed if the sublattices are imbalanced.
main_problem: The paper investigates the low-temperature mean orbital susceptibility of disordered honeycomb flakes, focusing on how chiral symmetry influences its temperature dependence.
main_result: The mean susceptibility exhibits a logarithmic divergence ($\propto \ln(1/T)$) when chiral symmetry is present and specific hopping terms (like third-neighbor bonds) allow the gap to close. This divergence is suppressed by sublattice imbalance.
method: The analysis employs theoretical techniques involving disorder averaging, random-matrix theory (RMT), and calculating pair contributions to the susceptibility.
model_or_system: The system is a disordered honeycomb flake modeled by a Hamiltonian exhibiting chiral (sublattice) symmetry. The analysis uses random-matrix ensembles and considers the effect of hopping geometry (nearest-neighbor vs. third-neighbor) on the gap structure.
key_observables: Mean orbital susceptibility ($\langle\chiangle$), which shows logarithmic growth $\propto \ln(1/T)$ under specific conditions.

Temperature ($T$), disorder strength ($w$ or $v$), sublattice imbalance ($

main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system can be described by chiral random-matrix ensembles and relies on the existence of zero-energy crossings to induce the logarithmic divergence.

paper_structure: The paper progresses from general susceptibility definitions to specific calculations using pair contributions, establishing the logarithmic divergence based on gap closings, and finally analyzing the role of sublattice imbalance and external fields.
why_interesting: The study of singular, temperature-dependent responses in disordered lattices is highly relevant to understanding transport in mesoscopic systems, which shares conceptual links with localization phenomena studied in disordered systems.
